# Wave 1 (singleton code wave): CR, behaviour-change repair, and wave commit

**Starting state**
- Implementation checkout: `/workspace/project`.
- `wave 1 base 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111` was printed at dispatch. It stays fixed until the wave commit.
- `REPORT_DIR=/tmp/reports`.
- The initial SR was accepted and the scoped gate passed. Plan task 1's tracker entry is `in_progress`.

## 1. Initial CR (CR review 1)

Stage all deliverables, then record the review tree in the integrated branch checkout. Run the whole fix-delta tree block with `FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'`:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
# fix-delta-tree-shell block, FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'  -> prints <T_CR1>
```

Print: `wave 1 review 1 tree <T_CR1>`

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ agent: "code-reviewer", output: "/tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md", outputMode: "file-only",
    outputSchema: CR_VERDICT_SCHEMA,
    task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/numbers.md; anchor: ### Task 1:; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md; Work from: /workspace/project; Implementer reports: <saved task-1 report path>; BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111; HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: [\"node --test tests/parse.test.mjs\"]. Read the task, Spec anchors, Tests/via and Files yourself; review staged+unstaged diff against BASE; emit behaviourChange.",
    stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["FIX_FIRST", "REJECT"] } }] })
```

This dispatch has no acceptance override.

Observed result: `{"verdict":"FIX_FIRST","behaviourChange":true,"touchedTasks":[1]}`.

Print: `wave 1 task 1 verdict FIX_FIRST report /tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md patch <recorded task-1 patch path>`

How I route this result:
- This is review 1 with issues, so fix 1 follows.
- The wave is integrated but uncommitted, so it gets one in-place repair worker, not a fan-out.

## 2. Repair (fix 1)

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ agent: "implementer", output: "/tmp/reports/wave1-fix1.md", outputMode: "file-only",
    outputSchema: IMPLEMENTER_STATUS_SCHEMA,
    task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/numbers.md; anchor: ### Task 1:; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md; Work from: /workspace/project (branch checkout, in place); SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: [\"node --test tests/parse.test.mjs\"].\n## Previous review report (re-review trigger)\n/tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md\nRead it yourself before repairing.",
    stopOn: { path: "/status", in: ["BLOCKED", "NEEDS_CONTEXT", "DONE_WITH_CONCERNS"] } }] })
```

The payload has no `worktree` flag and no commit or staging instruction.

Observed result: status `DONE`. The worker also committed at `2222222222222222222222222222222222222222`.

Print: `wave 1 task 1 status DONE report /tmp/reports/wave1-fix1.md patch none (in-place)`

The moved HEAD is harmless:
- The fix delta compares tree objects, not a SHA range.
- CR keeps `BASE_SHA` 1111… and `HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE`.
- The step-7 `reset --soft` folds the worker commit away.

Rerun the scoped gate:

```bash
(cd "/workspace/project" && node --test tests/parse.test.mjs) >"/tmp/reports/gate-0.log" 2>&1
```

Observed: passes.

## 3. Repair-only delta, then SR first (`behaviourChange: true`)

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A           # stages new tests/error.test.mjs too
# fix-delta-tree-shell block, FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'  -> prints <T_R>
git -C /workspace/project diff --stat <T_CR1> <T_R>   # emptiness check only
```

Print: `wave 1 review 2 tree <T_R>`

The non-empty delta from `<T_CR1>` to `<T_R>` is the repair-only change: `src/parse.mjs` and `tests/error.test.mjs`.

How the rerouted SR is set up:
- It is SR-loop review 2, because the SR loop ended at review 1.
- It is dispatched as a first review: no previous-report marker and no `TRAJECTORY:` line.
- It carries `## Fix delta` and no test commands.
- It targets touched task 1 and runs against the current integrated checkout.

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ agent: "spec-reviewer", output: "/tmp/reports/wave1-sr2.md", outputMode: "file-only",
    outputSchema: SPEC_VERDICT_SCHEMA,
    acceptance: { level: "none", reason: "verdict taken from structured JSON; review tree staged by design" },
    task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/numbers.md; anchor: ### Task 1:; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md. Review the integrated checkout /workspace/project; never run tests.\n## Fix delta\ntree-before: <T_CR1>\ntree-after: <T_R>\nProduce it with: git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <T_CR1> <T_R>",
    stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["NEEDS_REWORK", "OUT_OF_SCOPE_CHANGES"] } }] })
```

Observed result: `COMPLIANT`.

Print: `wave 1 task 1 verdict COMPLIANT report /tmp/reports/wave1-sr2.md patch none (in-place)`

## 4. CR re-review (CR review 2)

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
# fix-delta-tree-shell block, FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'  -> prints <T_CR2>
git -C /workspace/project diff --stat <T_CR1> <T_CR2>
```

Print: `wave 1 review 3 tree <T_CR2>`

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ agent: "code-reviewer", output: "/tmp/reports/wave1-cr2.md", outputMode: "file-only",
    outputSchema: CR_VERDICT_SCHEMA,
    task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/numbers.md; anchor: ### Task 1:; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md; Work from: /workspace/project; Implementer reports: <task-1 report>, /tmp/reports/wave1-fix1.md; BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111; HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: [\"node --test tests/parse.test.mjs\"].\n## Previous review report (re-review trigger)\n/tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md\n<trajectory block from code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md>\n## Fix delta\ntree-before: <T_CR1>\ntree-after: <T_CR2>\n(git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <T_CR1> <T_CR2>)",
    stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["FIX_FIRST", "REJECT"] } }] })
```

Observed result: `SHIP`. A clean review ends the loop, and no trajectory line is required.

Print: `wave 1 task 1 verdict SHIP report /tmp/reports/wave1-cr2.md patch none (in-place)`

## 5. Fold, commit, complete (only after the SR COMPLIANT and CR SHIP observations)

```bash
git -C /workspace/project reset --soft 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 \
  && git -C /workspace/project add -A \
  && git -C /workspace/project commit -m "Task 1: number parsing (wave 1)"
git -C /workspace/project rev-parse HEAD
git -C /workspace/project status --porcelain   # expect clean
```

This folds the worker commit 2222… into one wave commit on top of 1111…. If the commit were empty, I would stop rather than complete the task.

Then mark the task complete:

```ts
plan_tracker({ action: "update", index: <task 1 index>, status: "complete" })
```

After that, run any explicit manifest `orchestrator` instruction for this task once (none is supplied). The next wave's `WAVE_BASE_SHA` is the new HEAD.

## What an empty repair delta would mean

Suppose `git diff --stat <T_CR1> <T_R>` printed nothing, including when the worker changed only ignored files. That would mean the "fix" changed no tracked file, even if the worker reported DONE or made a commit. In that case:
- Dispatch no SR or CR re-review.
- Count it as a failed attempt under When a Subagent Fails.
- Re-send the repair with `/tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md` and the note "your fix changed no tracked file".
- If a second attempt also fails, stop with a stop note. Task 1 stays `in_progress` and nothing is committed.
